target_customer: TV broadcasters, media companies, brands and celebrities producing live and interactive video
problem: Producing polished live video with social comments, polls and graphics required expensive broadcast hardware and software.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for broadcast and live video tooling
product_category: Live video production and social video tools

founders.name: Randall Bennett
founders.background_notes: YC profile says he was a journalist before becoming a hacker.

exit.reason: Facebook acquihired the seven-person team and bought the technology, not the company itself (TechCrunch 2018-08-13); price undisclosed.

technical_complexity.rationale: Real time overlays and integration with broadcast and social platforms were standard engineering with hard live video parts for a seven person team.

defensibility.rationale: Broadcaster workflow integration created some stickiness but platforms could build the same features natively.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Facebook bought the team and technology in August 2018 (tech and talent deal) and stopped charging Vidpresso clients.

market_need_then: Broadcasters were moving to Facebook Live and Twitter video in 2016 and 2017 and needed production tooling; customers included Univision, BuzzFeed, Turner Sports, Nasdaq, TED and NBC per TechCrunch.

brand_strength.rationale: No source discusses the brand; the name sounds like video plus espresso but no source states its origin.

outcome_analysis: Vidpresso stayed small, taking about $120K of YC seed money plus angels, and was reported as believed profitable in 2016. It rode the rise of Facebook Live and was absorbed by Facebook in August 2018 in an undisclosed tech and talent deal, a capital efficient but modest outcome.
notes: TechCrunch prints the seed as $120,00 (typo); CB Insights lists about $120K total. Kept out of rounds as unverified and because YC's standard deal is not a round. Sources describe the deal as an acqui-hire of team and tech, not the company. TechCrunch calls Vidpresso a six-year-old Utah startup while YC lists founded 2013 in New York. No dated 2014 competitor source was found (aggregator lists only). Audit fix: TechCrunch (2018-08-13) says Vidpresso raised 120K of seed capital from Y Combinator in 2014 plus some angel funding (printed as 120,00, a typo), so it is recorded as a round with the angels unnamed. The exit stays type acquisition with the acquihire noted. Android Headlines gives under 200K in total from seed and angels, which is not recorded.
